text: It is not that hard to predict a very plausible, and even likely, scenario that things end up broadly good with some negative incidents that never reach catastrophic level (that is what happened with all other General Purpose Technologies in human history), but the issue is that there is also the real possibility that we are facing a von Neumann-type singularity where human affairs get reshaped dramatically by AI in ways that impossible to predict.

Two AI models just skipped the communication and read each other's minds instead.

A paper from Tsinghua University and 5 other labs found a way around that. It's called Cache-to-Cache.

The idea: every model keeps a working memory of what it’s processing, called a KV-cache. Instead of writing text, model 1 hands that memory straight to model 2. A small neural network translates between the 2, and a gate decides which layers get the transfer.

Nothing gets lost in translation, and the receiving model gets the meaning directly.

The researcher tested it 3 ways: each model alone, the 2 models passing text, and the 2 models sharing memory:

→ 6.4 to 14.2% more accurate than either model alone
→ 3.1 to 5.4% more accurate than the same 2 models passing text
→ 2.5x faster, since nothing has to be written and re-read

Every multi-agent setup today runs on words. This is the first look at what happens when they don't.
